summary: Walk-up adult fares are resolved from the National Rail RJFAF static fares feed synced into local SQLite via `fare sync`, not scraped or computed in-process; every location-expansion and flow-matching step (group members, clusters, CRS-to-NLC, flows, NDF overrides) must apply validity-date filtering with blank dates treated as open-ended (`col = '' OR col op ?`), and `fare` lookup falls back to the age-based freshness backstop instead of an authenticated probe when NR_OPENDATA credentials are absent.
reason: Replaces the retired ad hoc `internal/farescrape` HTML-scrape approach, which was fragile against site changes, with the official RJFAF feed as the source of truth. Date-filtering discipline exists because RJFAF group memberships, clusters, locations, and flows all carry validity windows; skipping any one of them let expired or not-yet-valid rows leak into or drop out of fare resolution for `--date` queries away from today (Greptile P1/P2 findings on resolve.go and store.go). The credential-optional freshness fallback exists because `fare sync` requires NR_OPENDATA creds but `fare` lookup against an already-synced store should stay usable offline/without creds rather than failing on an unauthenticated probe.
validated_outcome: go test ./... green for the full module including date-filtering regression tests (TestResolveExpiredGroupMembershipExcluded, TestResolveBlankFlowDatesIncluded, TestResolveBlankNDFDatesIncluded), the NDF group-NLC expansion test (TestResolveNDFGroupNLCOverride), and JSON-tag serialization tests. The NDF override step (Step 7) queries the same group/cluster-expanded location sets as flow-matching so overrides filed under a group NLC apply to member stations, and CRS-to-NLC resolution is deterministic (ORDER BY nlc). Live end-to-end smoke against the real RJFAF798 feed (53.8 MB) confirmed sync, offline lookup, and provenance/publish-date reporting. All Greptile review threads on PR #1341 resolved.
